properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From StoryFlow's principle #5, "Real-path tests — unit-green is not live-green": a test that feeds synthetic objects to a pure function proves the function is pure, and says nothing about whether anything calls it or whether the wire shape matches. Their worked case was a prose-rendering suite that was GREEN while the surface rendered no prose at all.

THEIR PROPOSED CHECK IS ALREADY COMPUTABLE HERE, WITH NO NEW VOCABULARY: "assert that each capability has at least one verification at `integration` or `system` level rather than `unit`."

MEASURED, 2026-08-22. Verification.level across 191 checks: integration 105, unit 72, system 11, acceptance 3. 154 capabilities carry a check; 47 of them are verified ONLY at unit level. The field has existed the whole time and NOTHING READS IT — no detector, no report, no rollup. That is the three-legs pattern with the tool and the data present and the detector missing, which is the same diagnosis as `change_axis_unstated` and cheaper to close, because no schema change is needed.

A SIBLING ALREADY EXISTS AND IS INSTRUCTIVE: `component_granularity_verification` fires when a capability is covered only by a check aimed at its COMPONENT rather than at itself — 9 capabilities here. That is the same argument on a different axis (WHAT is checked rather than HOW DEEP), and its existence is evidence the shape is acceptable in this design.

⭐ THE HONEST CAVEAT, and the document states it first: level is a PROXY. It does not measure path realism, it measures a label the author chose. A unit test can cross a real boundary and an "integration" test can mock everything. The document's own words — "cheap, and it makes the gap visible without pretending to measure path realism" — are the right register, and any finding must be worded that way or it will overclaim. This is also uncomfortably close to StoryFlow's own rule A(f): substituting a proxy that is easy to compute for the question actually asked.

AGAINST BUILDING IT: 47 of 154 is a third of the design, and a finding that fires on a third of everything on day one is a finding people filter. If built, aggregate — one question about the practice, not 47 about capabilities.
properties.name: OPEN — should a capability whose every check is `unit` level be a finding? 47 of 154 here, and the field is already recorded and never read
properties.no_relation_note: Searched 2026-08-22 on verification level and check granularity. Nearest were dec:component-verified-computed (ACCEPTED — component-granularity verification as a computed third state) and dec:idea-verification-is-planned-with-the-requirement (OPEN — planning a check when the need is stated). Both READ and judged NOT related in the relation vocabulary's sense: they are siblings arguing adjacent things about checks, not causes, dependencies or contradictions of this one. Component-granularity asks WHAT is checked; this asks HOW DEEP. Neither has to land first, neither blocks the other, and both could hold at once. Recorded as a note rather than a DEPENDS_ON, which would be false and would make a later reader think this waits on something. NOTE WRITTEN BY HAND because review_relations was not on this session's served tool surface.
properties.rationale: Recorded because it is the cheapest of the three mechanisms — the data is present, the field is populated, and only a reader is missing — and because its caveat is unusually clean: the proxy is admitted by the source that proposes it. Left open rather than proposed because a third of the design lighting up at once is a real adoption risk, and because whether a label-based proxy is worth having at all is a judgement about how much reflow2 should infer.
